data.name: Raaj
data.gender_notes: Raaj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who rules, governs or controls. Derived from the Sanskrit word 'Rājā' which means 'king'. The name Raaj carries the meaning “King, Ruler, Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Raaj usually hope their child will grow to embody king, ruler, sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner king or ruler, representing the individual's personal power and authority. Encourages self-rule, self-governance, and self-mastery.
data.etymology: Raaj belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King, Ruler, Sun.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raaj total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raaj holds a rich cultural significance in Hindu society, where names are associated with the divine and one's destiny. Raaj is a name that conveys power, authority, and leadership. It is often given to the eldest son or to those who are expected to lead and govern their families or communities. Raaj is a name that inspires respect and instills a sense of responsibility.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the soul is believed to be a divine spark that seeks to attain enlightenment and the ultimate goal of self-realization. The name Raaj holds a spiritual significance as it reminds us of the divine king within us. It is a reminder of our inner king, our higher self, and our innate ability to rule and govern our own inner world. The name Raaj calls us to step into our power and assert our own inner authority, guiding us towards greater self-awareness, personal growth, and spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raaj symbolizes regal power and wise rule. It represents the inner king, one who governs with compassion and righteousness. The name is a reminder to embody strength and authority in just and noble ways.

historical_references.reference: Raja Raja Chola I, also known as Rajaraja the Great, was a Chola king who ruled from 985 to 1014 CE. He is considered one of the greatest rulers in the history of the Chola Empire. He extended the Chola territory from southern India to Sri Lanka, and he undertook extensive temple construction and patronage.
historical_references.context: Chola Empire, Temple construction and patronage

historical_references.reference: Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a prominent Indian social and religious reformer who lived from 1774 to 1833. He is considered one of the pioneers of the Bengal Renaissance. He advocated for the abolition of the caste system, and he played a key role in the establishment of the Hindu Reform Movement.
historical_references.context: Indian social and religious reform, Abolition of caste system, Hindu Reform Movement

The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
